interface_notes.value: Heating to 1050 °C largely decreased the GND density of the hot-rolled microstructure, but considerable martensitic transformation during quenching caused volume expansion, still resulting in high GND densities of lath martensite and retained austenite.

phase_evolution.value: During holding at 1050 °C all martensite in the hot-rolled steel reversed into austenite; C and Mn diffusion into austenite increased the austenite volume fraction, giving more lath martensite at room temperature. Prior austenite grains grew up and prior austenite grain boundaries (PAGB) moved to δ-ferrite, thinning and segmenting the δ-ferrite bands into discontinuous grains. The high heating temperature lowered the Mn content of the reversed austenite, decreasing austenite stability and raising Ms; the higher cooling rate of water quenching than air cooling further inhibited α-ferrite transformation and raised Ms, so the martensite region of IQ-1050 was larger and retained austenite fewer at room temperature.

source.reason: The laminated microstructure of IQ-1050 consists of δ-ferrite bands and lath martensite lamellae; the discussion notes stress concentration prone at the δ-ferrite/tempered martensite interface. For IQ-1050 the δ-ferrite band/martensite interface is the dominant interphase boundary.
Results and discussion describe the phase evolution during 1050 °C holding and water quenching and the effect on the δ-ferrite/martensite interfaces and prior austenite grain boundaries of IQ-1050.

unmapped_findings: IQ-1050 yield-to-tensile ratio = 0.62 and product of strength and elongation (PSE) = 1.9 ± 0.4 GPa % (Table 3).

For IQ-1050, the density of block boundaries (boundaries with misorientation > 45°) was higher than that of austenitic grain (AG) boundaries, in contrast to HR; this increased block-boundary density contributed to the yield strength of IQ-1050, and the red block-boundary bar density was highest at IQ-1050 (a little above the 0.8 µm^-1 gridline) among all conditions (Fig. 8(b)).

IQ-1050 had a poorer tensile strength (929 ± 30 MPa) and ductility (2.0 ± 0.3 %); more lath martensite in IQ-1050 than HR contributed to its higher yield strength (575 ± 13 MPa) but readily induced stress concentration during deformation causing premature failure.
The GND densities of austenite in HR and IQ-1050 were similar (FCC ~8.37 ×10^14 /m^2 for HR and ~5.01 ×10^14 /m^2 for IQ-1050).
